title: Acceptable Macronutrient Distribution Ranges (AMDR) — Dietary Reference Intakes for Macronutrients (National Academies / IOM)
content: National Academies of Sciences (Institute of Medicine) Dietary Reference Intakes — Acceptable Macronutrient Distribution Ranges (AMDR) for adults: carbohydrate 45-65% of total energy, protein 10-35% of total energy, fat 20-35% of total energy. These ranges are associated with reduced risk of chronic disease while providing adequate intake of essential nutrients; intakes outside these ranges are associated with increased risk of insufficiency or, in the case of fat, potential displacement of essential nutrients.

title: Acceptable Macronutrient Distribution Ranges (AMDR) — Dietary Reference Intakes for Macronutrients (National Academies / IOM)
content: AMDR — Product implication: these are general-population sanity ranges, not sport-specific optimums — an active person's protein % of calories may reasonably sit at or above the AMDR's upper bound (e.g. a high-protein cut) without being unsafe, but a proposed macro split falling far outside these bounds (e.g. carbohydrate near 0% or fat near 0%) should be flagged as an outlier needing explicit justification, not silently accepted.
